title: When you're tired
hook: Dazhu's practice: when hungry, eat; when tired, sleep, and nothing added
tomorrow: so what made today good, and would you even notice?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Epictetus at sea: the weather, the sky's part. This week's lines come back in the games: they're having a day, the kitchen, sweep, saunter, waiting, the weather. Then the hardest plain day of all.
screen: `THE WEATHER.` → `A WEEK OF LINES COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: It's the end of a long week, and a practice can turn into one more item on a list nobody can face. A Chan Buddhist teacher was asked about exactly this kind of effort. A visiting master of the monastic rules asked Dazhu: do you still make an effort in your practice? Yes, said Dazhu. How? When I'm hungry, I eat. When I'm tired, I sleep. The visitor wasn't impressed. Everyone does that, he said.
screen: `ONE MORE ITEM ON THE LIST.` → `DO YOU STILL MAKE AN EFFORT?` → `WHEN TIRED, I SLEEP.` → `EVERYONE DOES THAT.`

segments.voice: Dazhu's answer: it isn't the same. When they eat, they don't just eat; they're full of a hundred demands. When they sleep, they don't just sleep; they're turning over a thousand schemes. That's the Chan teaching, the school called Zen in Japan: practice is doing the one thing you're doing, wholly, with nothing added. Dazhu wasn't bragging about naps. The visitor measured effort by how hard it looked; Dazhu measured it by whether anything extra came along. That's why it's harder than it sounds. The just is the whole practice. And it's good news on a tired day, because the practice doesn't have to be long to be whole. When the full sit is too much, this path keeps a one-breath version: one breath, breathed as just a breath, the same knowing breath from the rose-apple shade, only one of it. Not a failed session. A whole one. Then sleep, and just sleep.
screen: `THEY DON'T JUST EAT.` · `ONE THING, NOTHING ADDED.` · `NOT LONG, BUT WHOLE.` · `THEN SLEEP, AND JUST SLEEP.` · then, large: `ONE BREATH.`

segments.voice: Let this whole sit be the tired-day version. Take one breath, in and out, and know it as just a breath, nothing added. Then rest, and if another breath comes, let it be just that one too.
When you're tired: the day the practice shrinks instead of stopping. Dazhu's way: when tired, sleep, and just sleep.
Your line: one breath, with nothing added to it. Nine of fourteen, and now, rest.

screen: `DAY 1764 COUNTS.` → `ORDINARY DAYS · 9 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT MADE TODAY GOOD, AND WOULD YOU NOTICE?`

howItsDone: Chan and Zen students treat ordinary acts, eating and sleeping included, as practice when done wholly; people on this path keep a one-breath version for tired days.

fork.setup: a friend with a new baby says she's failed at meditation: she can't sit for long anymore. what fits Dazhu?
options: one whole breath, nothing added, is real practice; and when tired, rest wholly too.
she has failed: for Dazhu, the long daily sit is the only real practice.
she should wait until the baby is older; practice needs plenty of spare time.
fork.reveal: Dazhu's practice was eating when hungry and sleeping when tired, wholly. a practice can be short and still whole.

original.note: Chinese: meditation, the name of Dazhu's school; Zen is its Japanese name.

trapdoor: what you thought: on tired days, practice means skipping it or forcing it.
what it means: for Dazhu, practice is doing the one thing wholly, so even one breath can be whole.
what a scholar hears: the exchange with the visiting master appears in the Transmission of the Lamp; the word just is its hinge.
guess: a low day when the practice shrinks but stays
a medical sign you should see a doctor about
a reason to skip practice until next week

chat.says: two weeks of hospice, work, storm. i'm wiped. skipping my practice tonight, it feels like homework.
options: do the one-breath version: one breath, just a breath, like Dazhu's 'when tired, sleep.'
push through the full sit; Dazhu says real practice means effort even when exhausted.
skip it for a while; Dazhu says practice only counts on well-rested days.
chat.meaning: Dazhu said his practice was eating when hungry and sleeping when tired, with nothing added. A tired day's practice can be one whole breath.

tie.story: Asked about his effort, Dazhu said: when hungry I eat, when tired I sleep; others don't just eat or just sleep.
tie.friend: Zoe can take one whole breath tonight, then just sleep, instead of skipping or forcing it.

Dazhu.meaning: Dazhu Huihai, a Chinese Chan teacher known for plain answers

Chan.meaning: the Chinese school of Buddhism called Zen in Japan

Zen.meaning: the Japanese name for Chan, the meditation school of Buddhism
